extracted.intended_audience: general readers, researchers, journalists and students seeking a chronological account of incidents involving QAnon
extracted.subtask_description: Assemble and present a chronological, encyclopedic timeline of incidents tied to QAnon, summarizing each event with relevant facts and sources. The page compiles incident titles, dates, locations, actors, actions, legal outcomes, and citations, with links to fuller 'main article' entries when available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chronological organization by year and incident
rubrics_metrics.description: Events are grouped under year headings (e.g., 2018, 2019, 2020, etc.) with individual incident subheadings for each entry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use clear year-level sections and separate entries for distinct incidents so readers can follow the temporal progression; the page demonstrates this with headings like '2018', '2019', '2020 and later', and individual incident entries (e.g., 'Hoover Dam incident', 'Murder of Frank Cali').

rubrics_metrics.name: Concise incident title plus summary paragraph
rubrics_metrics.description: Each incident has a short descriptive heading followed by a concise paragraph summarizing what happened.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide an informative heading (often a short noun phrase) and one or more paragraphs that summarise the key facts — who, what, when, where, and immediate consequences — as shown throughout the page (e.g., 'Hoover Dam incident' followed by arrest, motive, and sentence details).

rubrics_metrics.name: Include actors, dates, locations, and motivations/context
rubrics_metrics.description: Entries specify the people involved (names/aliases), the date(s) or year, the geographic location, and the actor's stated or reported motivation or QAnon-related beliefs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document identity (or identifying details), place, timing, and linkage to QAnon beliefs or activities when relevant — for example, mentioning Matthew Phillip Wright of Henderson, Nevada, his actions at Hoover Dam, and his stated QAnon-related mission; include when a suspect's mental health or other movements are reported.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report legal/process outcomes and follow-up
rubrics_metrics.description: Where applicable, incidents include subsequent legal charges, convictions, sentences, expulsions, arrests, or other official outcomes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note charging decisions, trial results and sentences (e.g., Wright's terrorism conviction and seven-year sentence; Hurren's sentencing for weapons-related charges), and later developments such as arrests or sentencing updates; include dates of legal outcomes where available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cite reliable sources for each claim
rubrics_metrics.description: Statements and summaries are tied to footnoted references to news outlets, official statements, court records, or other reliable sources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Support factual assertions with inline citations; the page uses many footnotes (e.g., references to The Washington Post, The New York Times, BBC, court documents). Where a 'Main article' exists, link to it and cite its sources as well.

rubrics_metrics.name: Link to 'Main article' for major incidents and related topics
rubrics_metrics.description: When an incident has a fuller standalone article, the timeline provides a 'Main article' link to that dedicated page.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use 'Main article:' labels and hyperlinks (e.g., 'Main article: Frank Cali § Death', 'Main article: January 6 United States Capitol attack') to direct readers to more detailed coverage rather than duplicating long narratives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Neutral, factual tone with attribution
rubrics_metrics.description: Text presents events in neutral, descriptive language and attributes claims to sources or to the actors themselves rather than asserting unverified conspiratorial facts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid repeating conspiratorial claims as facts; attribute alleged beliefs or claims (e.g., 'believed', 'claimed', 'according to') and let citations establish provenance. The page frames QAnon-related assertions as beliefs held by adherents and cites reporting or legal records.
